note: Senior PM reference bands for core/senior_pm_review.py. Every band restates a figure the PM signed on 2026-09-23 or a row of the signed envelope table; nothing here is invented, and nothing here can change a calculated CPM duration.

governance.rule: A reference band is read-only. It never supplies, shortens, overrides or mutates a calculated CPM duration. A duration changes only through an approved scenario that re-solves the CPM.
governance.no_fabrication: Every band must carry a source_ref that resolves to a shipped file and key. load_benchmarks() raises when a band has no resolvable source_ref, so an unevidenced reference can never be presented as an evidenced one.
governance.no_overstatement: A band is described only as what its source_ref supports. It is never presented as a trade-body figure, a published national norm or a company norm, and it is never presented as a measured project actual.

provenance.origin: Derived one-to-one from the PM-signed L2 master-duration table and its signed envelope bands.
limitations: These bands restate figures the PM signed on 2026-09-23. They are not measured project actuals: this pack holds no completed-project duration record, and no calibration dataset has been built from one.

A band is one trade's signed duration at the reference plate. It is NOT an independent cross-check of the engine. The engine consumes the very same signed table, so a band can confirm that a trade was scheduled as the PM signed it; it cannot establish that the signed figure is achievable.

The Physical Construction band is the signed envelope band, quoted in site days, for the governing plate and floor row. The PM signed its low and its high; the typical value is the arithmetic midpoint of that signed range and is a derived summary, not a signed number.
Where the PM signed a floor and no ceiling, the upper bound is b0 and the band is degenerate (low equals high). A degenerate band flags upward drift; it does not assert a normal range.

Physical Construction is selected by area: the governing row is the smallest signed maximum area that covers the project. Area beyond the largest signed row yields no band and is reported as INSUFFICIENT_BENCHMARK_DATA rather than extrapolated.

This file contains no area-to-duration lookup, no completion-date target and no saving commitment. Bands are compared on the unit each band declares, so a site-day band is never compared against a Mon-Fri count.

Trade-body figures, published national norms and company norms are deliberately absent: none was verified for this pack, so none is stated. A reviewer who wants such a reference must supply its source, and it will be recorded as an input, not as a finding.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed envelope band for a micro project: up to the micro maximum area on a single floor.
benchmarks.notes: Compared against the engine site-calendar span of the physical construction phase. Never against a Mon-Fri count.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed envelope band for a single plate: up to two floors within one plate.
benchmarks.notes: This is the band the 3.10 regression baseline reports as IN_BAND for a single-plate office. Typical is the midpoint of the signed range.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed envelope band for two plates: up to three floors.
benchmarks.notes: Governs any project above the single-plate maximum area and up to the two-plate maximum area.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed envelope band for four plates: up to six floors.
benchmarks.notes: Governs any project above the two-plate maximum area and up to the four-plate maximum area.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed envelope band for a dual-campus project: up to sixteen floors.
benchmarks.notes: Governs any project above the four-plate maximum area and up to the dual-campus maximum area.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed envelope band for a three-tower headquarters: up to forty floors.
benchmarks.notes: The largest signed row. A project larger than this maximum area has no signed band and is reported as INSUFFICIENT_BENCHMARK_DATA.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed b_min 5 d and b0 5 d for site_setup, package mobilise, approval_state adjusted.
benchmarks.notes: The PM signed a floor of 5 d for temporary water, temporary power and site protection, and signed no ceiling, so the upper bound is b0. Degenerate band: it flags upward drift, it does not assert a normal range.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed b_min 8 d and b0 12 d for testing_commissioning, package commissioning, approval_state confirmed.
benchmarks.notes: Scales on floors. The signed band is the plan of record; the review compares the scheduled integrated-T&C block against it.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed b_min 3 d and b0 6 d for furniture, package ff_e, approval_state confirmed.
benchmarks.notes: The signed note binds this trade to the IAQ test sequence, so the band constrains placement only and never authorises changing the furniture date on its own.

benchmarks.basis: PM-signed b_min 4 d and b0 4 d for construction_cleaning, package close_out, approval_state adjusted.
benchmarks.notes: The signed close_out package also carries final_cleaning at the same signed 4 d. The engine raises no closeout_handover activity, so this band is stated and reported as not comparable until such an activity exists.
